headline: Today's sound headlines
lead: 30 new stories from 15 sound and audio news sources over the last 72 hours, including Sound On Sound, Production Expert, FOH, TPi, TV Technology and 10 more. This edition is assembled automatically from the outlets' own feeds: titles and summaries are theirs, sorted into sections. Open a story for the full article.

items.title: Shy Audio launch 80s Samplez & Mini bundle
items.take: With a collection of 1990’s home-studio hardware emulations already under their belt, Shy Audio have rolled the clock back a bit further and created two plug-ins based on the Akai S612.

items.title: PT EDL 3 Adds Multitrack Expand, Dialogue Search And Pro Tools PTX Conform
items.take: Free Range Audio has released PT EDL 3, a substantial rework of Pete Gates' Mac app for reconforming Pro Tools sessions and assembling sound rushes from an edit. It's built for dialogue editors, sound editors, and re-recording mixers who deal with picture recuts and turnovers.

items.title: Photophore 2, a 100-oscillator iOS/AUv3 flock synth twelve years in the making
items.take: Photophore renders a swarm of one hundred oscillators as a flock navigating a three-dimensional habitat. First seen on CDM in 2014, version 2 of Taika Systems' instrument adds AUv3 support on iOS -- and parameters modeling predators, hunger, and fear.

items.title: LIVE Green launches updated Clauses for artists booking contracts
items.take: LIVE Green has launched its updated template clauses for artist booking contracts, celebrating the continued use of sustainability clauses across the live music industry and making it easier for more artists and their teams to adopt green working practices.

items.title: Knightsnare offers KNS16 and Knightverb 2000 reverb plugins for FREE
items.take: Jonathan Knightsnare is offering KNS16 and Knightverb 2000, two free reverb plugins inspired by the AMS RMX16 and Lexicon Model 200. Both plugins mimic the keypad-driven workflow of early digital rack effects.

craft.body:
This week's dialogue debate comes down to one habit: judge the final mix on the system your audience will use. Before you print, play the key scenes on a TV or laptop at couch distance, at a normal home level, with captions off, and note every line you have to strain for.

Fix those on the dialogue, not with a blanket boost: a little more level on the line, less music or effects under it, or less compression on the bed. Keep a cheap TV or small speaker permanently wired into your monitor controller so this check costs you two minutes, not a trip to the living room.
craft.title: Do the last check where the audience listens
